record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the tenth International conference on fuzzy set theory and applications (FSTA 2010, Liptovsky Jan, Slovakia)
record.original_question: Describe the class C* of all binary operations obtained by transforming a bivariate copula C with a strictly increasing bijection phi:[0,1] -> [0,1] via C_phi(x,y)=phi^{-1}(C(phi(x),phi(y))). The description should account for the fact that such transforms need not be copulas and that the resulting class is strictly contained in the class of continuous semicopulas.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A bivariate copula is a function $C:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ satisfying (i) $C(x,0)=C(0,x)=0$ and $C(x,1)=C(1,x)=x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$, and (ii) the 2-increasing property $C(x_2,y_2)-C(x_2,y_1)-C(x_1,y_2)+C(x_1,y_1)\ge 0$ whenever $0\le x_1\le x_2\le 1$ and $0\le y_1\le y_2\le 1$. A continuous semicopula is a continuous function $S:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ that is non-decreasing in each argument and satisfies $S(x,1)=S(1,x)=x$ and $S(x,0)=S(0,x)=0$.

Given a strictly increasing bijection $\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ (necessarily continuous) and a copula $C$, define the transformed binary operation
$$C_\varphi(x,y)\;:=\;\varphi^{-1}\bigl(C(\varphi(x),\varphi(y))\bigr),\qquad (x,y)\in[0,1]^2.$$
Let
$$\mathcal C^* \;=\; \{\,C_\varphi : C\text{ is a bivariate copula and }\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]\text{ is a strictly increasing bijection}\,\}.$$
It is known that $C_\varphi$ need not itself be a copula and that $\mathcal C^*$ is strictly contained in the class of continuous semicopulas.

Problem: Give an intrinsic characterization of the class $\mathcal C^*$, i.e., describe necessary and sufficient conditions on a continuous semicopula $S:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ so that $S=C_\varphi$ for some bivariate copula $C$ and some strictly increasing bijection $\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$.
artifact.status_search_result: Related work by Durante and Sempi (2005) and subsequent papers studies properties preserved by the transformation $C_\varphi(x,y)=\varphi^{-1}(C(\varphi(x),\varphi(y)))$ on copulas, quasi-copulas, and semicopulas, and establishes strict inclusions. However, no source found provides a complete intrinsic characterization of the class $\mathcal C^*$ within the continuous semicopulas, so the status of the full description appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Copula and semicopula transforms (Durante–Sempi)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the transformation Ch(x,y)=h^{-1}(C(h(x),h(y))) on copulas, quasi-copulas, and semicopulas; shows several properties are not preserved.
status_evidence.claim: The transformation is studied but a full intrinsic characterization of the resulting class is not given.

status_evidence.title: On a class of transformations of copulas and quasi-copulas
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates inclusions among classes of transformed copulas and quasi-copulas.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial inclusion results but does not present a complete characterization of the transform class.
